deltas.description: Explicit h>=0 is mathematically necessary for the general one-step bound and is absent from the printed theorem restriction.

repairs.proposed_change: In Theorem3.3 replace the printed step restriction h<=1/beta with 0<=h<=1/beta. Retain the pinned source statement separately; do not overwrite it.
repairs.reconstructed_statement: In the source C2 Euclidean setting, let f be alpha-convex and beta-smooth. For every x,y and step size 0 <= h <= 1/beta, with T(z)=z-h grad f(z), ||T(y)-T(x)|| <= sqrt(1-alpha h)||y-x||. The source positive reciprocal and ordinary square-root domains remain unchanged; this proposal only makes the missing nonnegative-step restriction explicit.
repairs.justification: The literal all-real-step statement fails for every negative h on f(t)=t^2/2 with alpha=beta=1. The proof needs h>=0 when multiplying the curvature and step bounds.
repairs.minimality_evidence: Only add h>=0; include h=0 because T is then identity and the factor is 1. No strict positivity of h, no additional smoothness, and no dimension restriction is proposed. Existing reciprocal/square-root source domains are not redefined. Removing h>=0 admits the explicit quadratic counterexample.

reference_or_counterexample.counterexample: f(t)=t^2/2 on R, alpha=beta=1, h=-1, x=0,y=1: h<=1/beta but 2>sqrt(2). For every h<0, (1-h)^2-(1-h)=h(h-1)>0.
